div.head: CHn cor 5.1
div.ab: Si quis captus fuerit, siue monetarius siue alius, cum falsa moneta, iusticia recta inde fiat.
Si quis captus fuerit, sive monetarius sive alius, cum falsa moneta, iusticia recta inde fiat.
If a moneyer or any other person has been seized with false money, the process fitted to the case shall be carried out.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 278–279 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 522, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: Vgl. Gl Münzfälschung. Die Worte wiederholt Hn mon 2, ihren Sinn, aber vielleicht nicht aus Urkunden, sondern Justizhandhabung Rich. v. Hexham (ed. Howlett 141): falsae monetae factores et studiosos expensores gravi animadversione puniri fecit [Henricus I.]

Cf. Gl Münzfälschung. The words are repeated by Hn mon 2; their sense, though perhaps not from charters but from the administration of justice, is given by Rich. of Hexham (ed. Howlett 141): falsae monetae factores et studiosos expensores gravi animadversione puniri fecit [Henricus I.]
